title: Assistant gesture profiles — sketch
content:
Context / elevator
- Quick personal sketch for a small, incremental feature: let apps choose a lightweight ‘gesture profile’ when calling the API or within the Console UX. The profile controls high-level response behavior (verbosity, formality, hedging, emoji/markdown use, cite-style) without requiring prompt engineering on the app side.

Why this?
- Problem: product teams keep reinventing the same small output tweaks (short vs long, verbose vs terse, polite vs direct) by wrapping prompts or building brittle templates. This increases prompt maintenance and leads to inconsistent user experience across routes.
- Opportunity: expose a stable, easy-to-understand abstraction (a few named profiles) that maps to prompt / parameter transforms and runtime post-processing. Low friction for both product and infra.

High-level idea
- Add optional query param / SDK option: gesture_profile (string) with built-in values: concise, conversational, formal, assertive, playful, factual. Console UI: dropdown when configuring a route.
- Backend: small profile registry that expands to a short instruction template + post-process rules + token-cost guardrails. Keep profiles tiny (<= 3 short rules) so they’re obvious.
- Profiles are composable with model options (model_variant, temperature, safety_level). E.g., concise + high-temperature = concise but creative; formal + low-temperature = conservative formal.

Prototype mapping (example)
- concise -> prepend: "Respond in 1–2 short sentences; prioritize clarity; avoid filler." post-process: truncate to ~40–80 tokens; avoid leading filler words.
- conversational -> prepend: "Friendly, first-person, use contractions; keep answers clear; add a short example when helpful." post-process: allow slightly longer (100–180 tokens).
- formal -> prepend: "Use formal register; avoid slang; provide citations where applicable; close with a next-step suggestion." post-process: prefer more sentences.
- assertive -> prepend: "Be direct and confident. Provide a recommended action. Do not hedge unless safety risk." post-process: remove hedges (e.g., "might", "could").
- playful -> prepend: "Light, playful tone; optional emoji; one short joke allowed; still be helpful." post-process: allow emoji whitelist.
- factual -> prepend: "Concise factual answer. If uncertain, say 'I don't know' and suggest sources." post-process: stricter hallucination filter.

Open questions / risks
- Safety: assertive profile could increase risk of overconfident hallucinations. Need rules: assertive + safety_level=high triggers stricter citation heuristics.
- Cost: concise reduces tokens; conversational/playful increases tokens. Need to show token impact in Console and API usage meter.
- Complexity: too many profiles will confuse customers. Start small (3–4) and iterate.
- Interference with prompt engineering: some teams will want custom profiles; support is needed (customer-managed profiles in Dedicated/Private?).

UX sketch (Console / API)
- Console Route Editor: small dropdown labeled Response Gesture: [Default | Concise | Conversational | Formal | Assertive] + preview sample produced by selected model for a test prompt. Show delta on token estimate and example output.
- API: new optional param query string or body field: gesture_profile: "concise". SDK: Redwood.client.generate(..., {gestureProfile: 'concise'})
- Logging/observability: label traces and logs with gesture_profile value; expose per-profile metrics in Console (latency, token usage, quality regression flag).

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- API accepts gesture_profile param and applies profile mapping for hosted-api only.
- Console shows dropdown + small preview for model family gpt-*-like.
- Basic metrics instrumentation: token delta and 99p latency per-profile.
- Safety guardrail: assertive profile must enable hallucination-check hook; responses failing check return fallbacks.

Success metrics / experiments
- Adoption: percent of new routes that set a non-default gesture_profile within 8 weeks. Target: 10% in 8 weeks for top 50 active projects.
- Token impact: average tokens per response for concise vs default (expect -20%).
- Developer satisfaction: NPS-style quick survey in Console after using preview: helpfulness/usability.
- Regression: track quality regressions via existing eval/prompt sets per-profile. Low false-positive rate on safety checks.

Implementation notes / infra touchpoints
- Small profile registry service (could be a config table). Frontend reads the registry for dropdowns.
- Transformation pipeline: insert short prepended instruction and a post-process filter step (regex/heuristic/token clamp). Avoid heavy compute.
- Telemetry: tag requests with profile id; surface in tracing and cost reports.
- Rollout: feature-flagged per-account; start internal preview + a handful of early customers (solutions-eng) for feedback.

Experiment ideas (quick)
- A/B test default mapping: default->conversational or default->concise for specific customer segments and measure retention/engagement.
- Let team craft one custom profile (private) and measure time-to-setup vs custom prompt method.

To dos / next steps (me)
- [ ] Draft minimal registry schema and example mapping (Yardstick: <= 6 keys).
- [ ] Spike: implement prototype in local runtime: inject instruction + simple post-process clamp. Target: 1 day.
- [ ] Run 10 sample prompts across 3 models and document outputs (for Console preview).
- [ ] Open a ticket for infra instrumentation: JIRA: INF-1427 (placeholder).
- [ ] Sync with safety (Hanae) re: assertive profile rules — schedule 30m.
- [ ] Quick UX mockup in Figma or even static screenshot for route editor.

Random note: this is intentionally tiny and opinionated. Keep it narrow and visible in Console as a discoverable quality-of-life feature. If customers want full persona/role engines, that's a bigger lift (long-term roadmap).

Slack breadcrumbs: #prod-features (thread: gesture-profiles), pinned: sample outputs, early customer asks (Solutions eng).

Prompt examples to show in preview (test suite)
- Q: "How do I reset my password on AcmeCorp?" -> concise vs conversational vs assertive outputs for side-by-side.
- Q: "Summarize the attached meeting notes" -> formal vs playful comparison.

Notes to self: avoid using the term "persona" here — gesture should imply surface-level stylistic control, not deep behavioral or permissioning model.

End of sketch.
